docs.title: Home
docs.text:
ziviSpaceEcho

RE-201 inspired tape echo + spring reverb for REAPER / JSFX.

A musical tape-delay instrument for dub echoes, unstable motor textures, spring ambience and hands-on cabinet-style performance.

REAPER JSFX Tape Echo Spring Reverb Mouse-only Editor Download JSFX Installation Complete Manual GitHub

Independent inspired-by project

ziviSpaceEcho is not an official emulation and is not affiliated with Roland, Boss, Cockos, REAPER or any trademark holder.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
ziviSpaceEcho is a REAPER JSFX plugin for dub echoes, tape-delay textures, spring reverb ambience and unstable motor-style modulation.

It combines a multi-head tape echo model, a parallel spring reverb branch, a custom green cabinet interface and a mouse-only parameter editor designed specifically for REAPER workflows.

docs.title: Core features
docs.text: Multi-head tape echoThree virtual playback heads with a 12-position mode selector. Spring reverb branchParallel reverb branch with dwell, decay, drip, bounce and grain. Motor behaviorRepeat-rate motor timing, manual ms, tempo sync and tap tempo. Tape characterDrive, noise, tape condition, formula, age and loop length. Premium cabinet UICustom green hardware-style interface with circular knobs and LEDs. Mouse-only editorNumeric modal editor designed to avoid REAPER shortcut conflicts.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
ziviSpaceEcho is written as a REAPER JSFX effect using EEL2 syntax.

Main source file:

src/ziviSpaceEcho.jsfx

Versioned source file:

src/ziviSpaceEcho_v7_6_2.jsfx

Legacy alias:

src/SpaceEcho_RE201_STABLE.jsfx

docs.title: Architecture summary
docs.text:
The plugin is organized around:

  • @init initialization;
  • @slider parameter updates;
  • @block timing and state updates;
  • @sample DSP processing;
  • @gfx custom graphical interface.

docs.title: DSP design notes
docs.text:
Core design ideas:

  • one virtual tape path;
  • multiple read heads;
  • parallel spring branch;
  • echo tone shaping separate from reverb tone shaping;
  • safety clamps for memory/time behavior;
  • final soft clipping.

docs.title: UI design notes
docs.text:
The custom UI uses:

  • responsive virtual canvas;
  • cabinet-style paneling;
  • circular controls;
  • LED indicators;
  • bottom control strip;
  • mouse-only modal editor.

The mouse-only editor avoids hardware keyboard capture because REAPER may route key events to host commands.

docs.title: Known JSFX constraints
docs.text:
Be careful with:

  • function ordering;
  • string operations;
  • keyboard capture;
  • @gfx parser behavior;
  • drawing functions such as gfx_gradrect, which always draw rectangular areas.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Download:
src/ziviSpaceEcho.jsfx
  1. Open REAPER.
  2. Choose:
Options → Show REAPER resource path in explorer/finder
  1. Open the Effects folder.
  2. Copy ziviSpaceEcho.jsfx into the Effects folder.
  3. Restart REAPER or refresh the FX browser.
  4. Search for ziviSpaceEcho in the FX browser.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Replace the old .jsfx file with the new version.

For active projects, keep old versioned files if a project depends on a specific build.

docs.title: The plugin does not appear
docs.text:
Try:

  • refresh the FX browser;
  • check that the file extension is .jsfx;
  • confirm the file is inside REAPER's Effects folder;
  • restart REAPER.

docs.title: The graphic UI does not show
docs.text: Use the plugin's UI Mode slider or REAPER's native UI option.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts interfere with editing
docs.text: Use the mouse-only modal editor. Do not use the physical keyboard for parameter entry.

docs.title: 1. Concept
docs.text:
ziviSpaceEcho is a musical tape echo and spring reverb instrument for REAPER.

It follows the workflow of a classic multi-head tape echo unit:

  1. audio enters a preamp / record stage;
  2. the signal is written to a virtual moving tape;
  3. multiple playback heads read the tape at different positions;
  4. selected heads are mixed according to the mode selector;
  5. repeats are shaped by tone, filtering, age, drive and feedback behavior;
  6. a spring reverb branch can run in parallel with the echo.

The goal is not strict component-level emulation. The goal is a playable, expressive and stable tape-delay instrument with the same kind of musical decision space: head selection, motor behavior, tape condition, echo intensity, spring ambience and hands-on cabinet-style control.

docs.title: 2.1 Header
docs.text: The top header identifies the plugin and includes the UI mode button.

docs.title: 2.2 Mode / Routing
docs.text:
The left section contains:

  • 12-position mode selector;
  • active head/reverb indicators;
  • timing mode selection;
  • output and stereo mode controls.

docs.title: 2.3 Main parameter grid
docs.text:
The main grid contains the core continuous parameters:

  • Echo / Mix
  • Tape Tone
  • Input Stage
  • Motor / Wow-Flutter
  • Filters
  • Spring Tank
  • Reverb Shape

docs.title: 2.4 Bottom control strip
docs.text:
The bottom strip contains discrete switches:

  • Input
  • Loop
  • Tape Formula
  • Tape Age
  • LFO Wave
  • Instrument Switch
  • Echo Cancel
  • Transport

It also displays dynamic timing information:

IPS | H1 ms | H2 ms | H3 ms

docs.title: 2.5 Mouse-only parameter editor
docs.text:
Click a numeric value below a knob to open the editor.

The editor includes:

  • selected parameter name;
  • current value;
  • default;
  • min and max;
  • numeric keypad;
  • decimal point;
  • contextual sign toggle;
  • DEL;
  • CLR;
  • DEFAULT;
  • CANCEL;
  • APPLY.

The editor intentionally avoids the hardware keyboard because REAPER may route keyboard shortcuts to the host rather than the JSFX window.

docs.title: RE-201 Motor
docs.text:
Uses Repeat Rate as a motor-speed style parameter.

Best for:

  • classic tape echo gestures;
  • performance-style speed changes;
  • non-grid rhythmic echoes.

docs.title: Manual ms
docs.text:
Uses Manual Time as the leading head delay time.

Best for:

  • precise delay design;
  • sound design;
  • matching a specific delay time.

docs.title: Tempo Sync
docs.text:
Uses the selected sync division.

Best for:

  • production work;
  • locked rhythmic patterns;
  • grid-based electronic music.

docs.title: Tap Tempo
docs.text:
Uses tap tempo for performance input.

Best for:

  • live playing;
  • quickly following a piece without calculating BPM.

docs.title: 4. Mode selector
docs.text:
Position Label Meaning 1 H1 Head 1 only 2 H2 Head 2 only 3 H3 Head 3 only 4 H2 + H3 Heads 2 and 3 5 H1 + Rev Head 1 plus reverb 6 H2 + Rev Head 2 plus reverb 7 H3 + Rev Head 3 plus reverb 8 H1 + H2 + Rev Heads 1 and 2 plus reverb 9 H2 + H3 + Rev Heads 2 and 3 plus reverb 10 H1 + H3 + Rev Heads 1 and 3 plus reverb 11 H1 + H2 + H3 + Rev All heads plus reverb 12 Reverb Only Spring reverb only

Position 12 uses a blue LED to visually separate reverb-only mode from amber echo positions.

docs.title: 5. Recommended starting levels
docs.text:
Intensity: 25–45%
Echo Volume: 35–55%
Reverb Volume: 15–35%
Drive: 5–20%
Noise: 0–12%
Condition: -10 to +20

Increase Intensity carefully when using longer times or multiple heads.

docs.title: 6. Mouse-only editing workflow
docs.text:
1. Click the numeric value below a knob.
  2. The modal editor opens.
  3. Enter the target value using the on-screen keypad.
  4. Click APPLY.

To reset:

  1. Click the numeric value.
  2. Click DEFAULT.

To cancel:

  1. Click CANCEL.

To correct entry:

  • DEL removes the last numeric input.
  • CLR clears the entry.

docs.title: 7. UI mode
docs.text:
The plugin includes a UI mode parameter:

  • Graphic Skin
  • Native Controls

Use native controls if you need standard REAPER automation editing or a fallback UI.

docs.title: Mode and timing
docs.text: Control Range / Values Description Mode Selector 1–12 Selects playback heads and reverb routing. Timing Mode Motor / Manual / Sync / Tap Selects the delay-time strategy. Repeat Rate 0–100% Motor-speed style control. Manual Time 20–2000 ms Leading head time in manual mode. Sync Division 2/1 to 1/32 Tempo-synchronized division.

docs.title: Echo / Mix
docs.text: Control Default Description Intensity 35% Feedback/repeat intensity. Echo Volume 45% Echo branch output level. Reverb Volume 22% Spring reverb branch output level.

docs.title: Tape tone
docs.text: Control Default Description Bass 0 dB Echo-only bass tone shaping. Treble 0 dB Echo-only treble tone shaping. Drive 10% Preamp/tape drive amount. Noise 8% Tape noise amount.

docs.title: Input stage
docs.text: Control Values Description Input Instrument / P.A. Send / Mic Input behavior selection. Input Level -24 to +18 dB Record/input gain. Instrument Echo Switch Echo / Dry Instrument echo behavior. Echo Cancel FX On / Cut Effect cancel behavior.

docs.title: Motor / Wow-Flutter
docs.text: Control Range Description Condition -100 to +100 General tape/machine condition. W/F Discrepancy -100 to +100 Wow/flutter discrepancy behavior. Motor Torque -100 to +100 Motor response/torque character. LFO Depth 0–100% Tape speed LFO modulation depth. LFO Rate 0.05–12 Hz Tape speed LFO rate. LFO Wave Sine / Triangle / Ramp / Square / Random Tape speed modulation waveform.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Control Range Description Low Cut -100 to +100 Playback head low-cut behavior. High Cut -100 to +100 Playback head high-cut behavior.

docs.title: Tape media
docs.text: Control Values Description Tape Formula Ampex 456 / 3M 996 Tape formula voicing. Tape Age New / Old Tape age voicing. Loop Length 36 / 72 / 120 in Virtual tape-loop length behavior.

docs.title: Spring tank
docs.text: Control Default Description Dwell 35% Excitation/drive into spring branch. Decay 45% Spring tail length. Drip 20% Spring drip/transient character. Bounce 35% Spring movement/bounce. Grain 30% Granular spring texture.

docs.title: Reverb shape
docs.text: Control Default Description Reverb Bass 0 dB Bass shaping for spring branch. Reverb Treble 0 dB Treble shaping for spring branch.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Control Values Description Output L / M / H Output-level behavior. Stereo Mode Single / Dual Original-like single mode or dual stereo mode. Master -24 to +12 dB Final output gain.

docs.title: Classic vocal slap
docs.text:
Mode: 1 or 5
Timing: Manual ms
Manual Time: 90–140 ms
Intensity: 10–25%
Echo Volume: 20–40%
Drive: 5–15%
Noise: 0–8%

docs.title: Dub feedback wash
docs.text:
Mode: 8, 9, 10 or 11
Timing: RE-201 Motor
Intensity: 55–85%
Echo Volume: 45–70%
Bass: +1 to +4 dB
Treble: -2 to -6 dB
Condition: +10 to +40
W/F: +10 to +35

Ride Repeat Rate and Intensity carefully.

docs.title: Ambient spring echo
docs.text:
Mode: 7, 8, 9 or 11
Reverb Volume: 35–65%
Dwell: 35–60%
Decay: 50–80%
Drip: 10–35%
Bounce: 25–55%
Grain: 20–45%

docs.title: Dirty tape loop
docs.text:
Drive: 25–55%
Noise: 12–30%
Condition: +35 to +70
Tape Age: Old
Loop Length: Short or RT-1
High Cut: negative values

docs.title: Clean production delay
docs.text:
Timing: Tempo Sync
Intensity: 20–40%
Echo Volume: 30–50%
Drive: 0–10%
Noise: 0–5%
Condition: -20 to 0
Stereo Mode: Dual

docs.title: Reverb only
docs.text:
Use position 12.

Mode: 12 Reverb Only
Reverb Volume: as needed
Dwell: 20–50%
Decay: 35–75%
Drip: 5–30%

Position 12 is marked with a blue LED.
